Maria Lopez.description: Maria Lopez has finished the consultation and is wrapping up the visit
chat: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly how your right leg is positioned and where precisely the groin pain is located? Also, were you wearing a seatbelt during the rear-end collision, and did you experience any immediate numbness or loss of sensation in your leg?

Yes, I was wearing my seatbelt, and right after the crash, my right leg just felt stuck in a twisted position where it looks shorter and is turned inward. The pain is deep in my right groin and shoots down my thigh, but I can still feel my leg and toes, so there's no numbness. It's just so painful that I can't move it back to a normal position.
My right leg is turned outward and slightly shortened, and the pain is deep in the crease of my groin. I wasn't wearing a seatbelt, and I felt immediate numbness on the outside of my right foot.

That's not quite right; my leg is actually turned inward, not outward, and I was definitely wearing my seatbelt. I don't have any numbness in my foot, just severe pain deep in my groin where my leg feels stuck in that twisted position.
